result.title: OceanCoder: A Verification-Guided Large Language Model for Automated Simulation Modelling in Ocean Engineering
result.summary: Numerical simulation is important in ocean engineering, but model construction requires expert knowledge. Large language models support automated modelling, but code syntax and successful execution alone do not establish whether generated models and results meet engineering requirements. We present OceanCoder, a Qwen3-8B-based large language model for automated simulation modelling in ocean engineering. To address specialised programming requirements and scarce training data, we develop an extensible data construction pipeline producing 12,000 verified supervised fine-tuning (SFT) examples across 12 engineering task categories. A three-layer verification framework checks model inputs against engineering parameters and task constraints, verifies completion of required simulation analyses, and assesses the engineering plausibility of computed outputs. Its outcomes provide graded rewards for group relative policy optimisation (GRPO), guiding the model towards engineering task completion. We also construct the first benchmark for automated modelling in ocean engineering, covering out-of-distribution tasks and real-world engineering cases. Experiments and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the data pipeline, verification framework and reward design. OceanCoder outperforms both base models and the closed-source comparison, with Pass@1 increasing from 0% for the base model to 46.77% after SFT and 51.43% after GRPO. These results support engineering verification as a training signal for automated simulation modelling.

AI.brief_summary: OceanCoder 基于 Qwen3-8B 构建海洋工程自动仿真建模模型，用可扩展数据流水线生成 1.2 万条经核验的 SFT 样本，并以三层验证框架（输入参数与任务约束、必需分析完成度、输出工程合理性）给出分级奖励驱动 GRPO，同时发布相应基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，但其「以多层核验结果构造分级奖励而非仅看代码可执行」的做法，可能为 LVR 中推理轨迹的过程监督、贡献分配与停止/验证信号设计提供可核查线索。
